title: AI 如何解锁新颖的游戏机制

How AI is Unlocking Novel Game Mechanics
Skip to content
AI x Gaming
How AI is Unlocking Novel Game Mechanics
By Max Abrahamsen •   September 1, 2026
Source: Naavik
The relationship between game development and AI has been uneasy at times, especially with concerns around generative AI driving raw content output. Fewer concerns emerge when technology enables new forms of creativity, making projects that were unrealistic in the past achievable today — especially if it enables smaller developers to pursue a unique creative vision.
This week, we’ll look at MIMESIS, Death by AI, and Status, three very different games that place AI directly inside their core gameplay loops in new ways.
What are the core mechanics? How are the games performing? What does it signal about the future? Let’s dive in and find out!
MIMESIS
Source:
ReLU Games
Developer:
ReLU Games
Platform:
Steam
Monetization: Paid early access ($9.99)
Released: October 27, 2025
Established in 2023 as an independent studio under
KRAFTON
, ReLU Games built its studio identity entirely around leveraging AI and deep learning to make games. This makes sense and reflects KRAFTON’s recent heavy investment in AI. MIMESIS has become ReLU Games’ biggest commercial success, surpassing 2M cumulative sales by July 2026,
according to KRAFTON
.
Source:
2024-KRAFTON-ESG-Report
The game is a four-player co-op survival horror game with an inspired core mechanic. The Mimesis (enemy) mimics players across two dimensions: behavior (using AI models that react to in-game context) and voice (by recording players through their microphones and replaying appropriate snippets later).
During play, voice lines are recorded and used during the session; they are not generated by AI (
according to the developer
); instead, AI is used to decide when and how to deploy those recorded voice lines. Rather than replaying clips randomly, ReLU says the system evaluates the conversation and game state and selects lines that fit the situation, making the imitation more convincing. ReLU says the
AI is deliberately trained to produce varied behavioral responses
to the same situation rather than following one fixed behavioral pattern — for example, one Mimesis might fight while another retreats.
This effectively changes the usual co-op horror experience from simply being about “where is the monster?” to “is that actually my teammate?” This creates a sense of dread as the familiar turns unfamiliar and unlocks a set of game mechanics that are difficult to achieve convincingly with traditional scripted NPCs. In essence, MIMESIS does something different. It doesn’t just use AI to make an easily identifiable game mob more interesting; it uses AI to obfuscate who is friend or foe, and this causes players to invent entirely new behaviors themselves.
However, the game’s main selling point is also a point of criticism: players comment that the AI is not robust enough
to deliver on the premise
. The game’s lifetime MAUs show a surge in user activity during the launch quarter — peaking at 562K in December 2025 — a level the developers haven’t managed to recapture. Additionally,
ReLU itself said
the Early Access release lacked enough maps, monsters, and equipment to sustain repeat play, making the drop in user interest more than an AI problem.
MIMESIS MAUs | Source:
Sensor Tower
It’s worth asking: how long does the deception remain effective
once players understand the system
? Horror mechanics based on uncertainty can lose power once players develop reliable counter-strategies or become accustomed to hearing reused voice lines. The long-term design challenge is whether ReLU can preserve uncertainty once experienced players understand the rules.
Still, MIMESIS is an interesting example of KRAFTON’s broad AI strategy. While much of the industry’s AI investment is focused on improving development efficiency, KRAFTON has also explicitly pursued AI as a source of game innovation, using it to explore new forms of gameplay. Additionally, MIMESIS was developed roughly two years ago, which is an eternity in the world of AI. As such, MIMESIS should be perceived more as an early signal of player interest rather than a definitive example of AI’s technical capabilities.
Death by AI
Source: Death by AI
Developer:
Little Umbrella Games
Platforms:
Discord
,
Web
,
iOS
Monetization model: F2P with IAPs
Released: December 2023
Little Umbrella Games is focused on building social AI games, with its first title, Death by AI, becoming an immediate breakout hit. The game took off quickly after launching on Discord in May 2024, reaching more than
20M players within the first three months
. That success subsequently helped Little Umbrella raise a $2M seed round in January 2025 to expand its portfolio of AI-powered social games.
Death by AI is a prompt-based game with a core mechanic that is deceptively simple. Players are dropped into a deadly scenario (like being cornered by a venomous snake) and given 60 seconds to explain how they intend to survive. There are no predefined actions to choose from; instead, players have total freedom to write exactly how they plan to escape. They can type whatever they want — whether ridiculous, clever, or elaborate — after which an AI Game Master interprets the response and decides whether the player lives or dies. The AI Game Master also graciously explains exactly how their fate unfolds.
Source:
Imgur
Traditionally, games have operated inside a fixed action space where the designer determines what a player is allowed to do and what the corresponding outcomes are. Death by AI replaces those fixed boundaries with interpreted outcomes, significantly expanding both action and outcome space. The core mechanic also creates an interesting second game hidden underneath the first. Players are not only trying to solve the scenario but are also trying to convince the AI that their solution should work. The developers themselves describe the core loop as “tricking the AI to let you live.”
